editorial:
Ever felt like you were totally stuck on one person for way too long? You will relate to Yoshika, a young office worker who has been obsessed with a guy named Ichimiya since middle school. She calls him the One and has basically blocked out every other man in her life for years. The vibe is super light and quirky, focusing on that awkward feeling of having a crush that takes over your whole brain. It is a funny look at how love can sometimes feel more like a hobby or a mission than a real relationship.

The acting is great because it captures those cringey, relatable moments of being socially awkward. The pacing is snappy, and the plot twists keep you guessing about whether she will actually get her guy. One downside is that it feels a bit short, but that just makes it an easy watch. If you love cute rom-coms, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: After all her planning and obsession, Yoshika finally realizes that her dream version of Ichimiya isn't who he actually is. She learns that chasing a fantasy isn't the same as having a real connection. Instead of sticking to her old crush, she opens her heart to the coworker who actually cares about her. It wraps up with her letting go of the past and choosing a healthier, more realistic kind of love.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky Japanese rom-coms and stories about first loves.
